extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A benchmark corpus for question answering research containing real anonymized, aggregated Google search queries paired with Wikipedia pages and human-annotated long and short answers.
extraction.creator: Google Research
extraction.citeAs: Kwiatkowski, T., Palomaki, J., Redfield, O., Collins, M., Parikh, A., Alberti, C., Epstein, D., Polosukhin, I., Devlin, J., Lee, K., Toutanova, K., Jones, L., Kelcey, M., Chang, M.-W., Dai, A. M., Uszkoreit, J., Le, Q., & Petrov, S. (2019). Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 7, 453–466. https://doi.org/10.1162/tacl_a00276
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected from real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine by multiple users in a short period of time. Simple heuristics filtered the query stream to retain questions of 8 words or more, and the queries were run through Google search to keep those with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 results. Annotators then labeled long and short answers using a custom annotation interface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Both long and short answers can be NULL if no viable candidates exist on the Wikipedia page. The paper also notes that the information required to answer may be spread across many paragraphs, in which case annotators mark no answer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated Google search queries and the corresponding Wikipedia pages returned in the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Queries were filtered with heuristics to discard non-questions and retain longer questions; questions were run through Google search and only those with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 results were kept.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were restricted to queries of 8 words or more and sampled using heuristic patterns; examples without a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A pool of around 50 annotators used a custom annotation interface. Each annotator completed three stages in succession: question identification (good/bad), long answer identification (select earliest HTML bounding box containing enough information or mark no answer), and short answer identification (select entity or set of entities within the long answer, or mark yes/no/NULL). The public release includes single annotations for training and 5-way annotations for development and test data; 25-way annotations were collected on a subset to study variability.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was evaluated post hoc using consensus judgments from four experts and by 5-way and 25-way annotations. The paper distinguishes correct, correct-but-debatable, and wrong answers, and analyzes variability across annotators and agreement with expert judgments.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Training examples: 1; development data: 5; test data: 5; variability study subset: 25
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A pool of around 50 annotators; no further demographics reported.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Google search engine; Google Cloud NLP API; TF-IDF weighted word overlap used in a baseline copying method; Hearst patterns were used to define categorical noun phrases.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Anonymized aggregated user queries; no explicit collection of other sensitive human attributes is reported.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to drive research in natural language understanding and question answering, with potential utility to users. The paper frames it as a benchmark for improving QA systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that using Wikipedia as the source may introduce biases, and that future collection efforts may include shorter queries, 'how to' questions, or domains other than Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions are limited to longer queries and to those with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results. The dataset focuses on Wikipedia and may not generalize to other domains. The paper also notes ambiguity and variability in acceptable answers, especially for naturally occurring questions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and test benchmarking for question answering research; evaluation of long-answer and short-answer extraction systems; study of human performance and annotation variability.
